doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Closing reflections
summary: Mandel closes by saying he is proud to be part of the American songwriting tradition and lucky to have spent his life doing what he loves.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Boy, it’s wonderful just to be among all that and to be able to – we have such great literature to – you know this is the great treasury of American art, is the songwriting that has come out of this century of American music. And I’m just very proud to even however remotely, be associated with it.
Well, it’s far more than remotely as any number of people I think would attest.

Well, it’s an honor I’ll tell you that. And most of all to be able to have spent your life doing something you love, what more can you ask for? You know, that’s the most anybody can ask for and I was lucky enough to have it, and it ain’t over yet. Not by a long shot.
Unless you have something to add I couldn’t come up with a better ending line than
I think that wraps it up. Thank you very much.
